description: Learn essential HTTP security headers: Content Security Policy (CSP), HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, and Referrer-Policy.

slides.title: Introduction to HTTP Security Headers
slides.content:
# HTTP Security Headers 🛡️📜

Modern web browsers ship with powerful security capabilities, but they remain dormant unless your web server explicitly activates them.

**HTTP Security Headers** are response headers returned by your web server that instruct the browser how to behave when handling your site's content.

## Key Headers in this Module:
- **Content-Security-Policy (CSP)**: The ultimate defense against XSS and data exfiltration
- **Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS)**: Forcing HTTPS and preventing SSL stripping
- **X-Frame-Options**: Guarding against UI clickjacking
- **X-Content-Type-Options**: Neutralizing MIME-type confusion attacks
- **Referrer-Policy**: Preventing leakage of sensitive URLs and tokens
- **Permissions-Policy**: Restricting browser hardware APIs (camera, geolocation, microphone)

slides.title: Content Security Policy (CSP) Anatomy
slides.content:
# Content Security Policy (CSP) 📜

**Content Security Policy (CSP)** is an HTTP response header that restricts which dynamic resources (scripts, styles, images, fonts, connections) the browser is allowed to load and execute.

## Anatomy of a CSP Header

A CSP header consists of semicolon-separated directives, each followed by allowed sources:

```http_not
Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://trustedscripts.com; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: https:;
```

## The Fallback: `default-src`

The `default-src` directive acts as a fallback for all unspecified resource directives (e.g. if `media-src` is omitted, it inherits `default-src`).

slides.content: # Core CSP Directives Reference 🧭 | Directive | Governs | Example Value | |---|---|---| | `script-src` | JavaScript execution and script tags | `'self' https://cdn.jsdelivr.net` | | `style-src` | CSS stylesheets and `

slides.title: Nonces and Hashes in CSP
slides.content:
# Strict CSP: Nonces & Hashes 🎲

Using `'unsafe-inline'` destroys XSS protection. How can you allow legitimate inline scripts while blocking attacker injections?

## 1. Cryptographic Nonce (`nonce-{random}`)

A **nonce** is a cryptographically strong, random, single-use string generated by the server on **every request**:

```http_not
Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'nonce-R4nd0mStr1ng123';
```

```html_not
<!-- Allowed because the nonce matches the header: -->
<script nonce="R4nd0mStr1ng123">
  console.log('Legitimate inline script executes!');
</script>

<!-- BLOCKED: Attacker injected script lacks the secret per-request nonce! -->
<script>alert('Hacked')</script>
```

## 2. SHA Hashes (`'sha256-...'`)

Whitelist the exact cryptographic hash of the script body content.

slides.title: CSP Reporting: Report-Only Mode
slides.content:
# Safe Rollout: `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` 📊

Deploying CSP on an existing large application can easily break legitimate styles or third-party analytics.

## The Report-Only Header

The `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` header tests your policy **without blocking any resources**! Violations are sent to a reporting endpoint as JSON:

```http_not
Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; report-to /csp-violation-report-endpoint
```

## Sample Violation Report JSON

```json
{
  "csp-report": {
    "document-uri": "https://example.com/checkout",
    "blocked-uri": "https://untrusted-analytics.com/tracker.js",
    "violated-directive": "script-src 'self'"
  }
}
```

slides.title: HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS)
slides.content:
# HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) 🔒

Even if your site redirects HTTP to HTTPS, the initial request (`http://example.com`) travels unencrypted over port 80. An attacker can perform **SSL Stripping** to downgrade the connection.

## Enter HSTS (`Strict-Transport-Security`)

HSTS tells the browser: *"For the next year, never connect to this domain over HTTP. Automatically convert all requests to HTTPS before sending them over the network!"*

```http_not
Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload
```

## Directives Explained:
- `max-age=31536000`: Cache this rule for 1 full year (in seconds).
- `includeSubDomains`: Applies HTTPS enforcement to all subdomains (`api.`, `mail.`).
- `preload`: Qualifies the domain for inclusion in browser hardcoded HSTS Preload Lists (Chrome, Firefox, Safari).

slides.title: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
slides.content:
# MIME Sniffing Prevention: `nosniff` 👃

Historically, browsers tried to be "helpful" by ignoring the server's declared `Content-Type` header and inspecting the file's raw bytes (**MIME sniffing**).

## The Attack Vector

1. Attacker uploads an avatar image (`avatar.jpg`) that actually contains malicious JavaScript inside its metadata.
2. When requested, the browser ignores `image/jpeg`, detects JavaScript code, and executes it as a script!

## The Fix: `X-Content-Type-Options`

```http_not
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
```

This forces the browser to strictly honor the server's declared MIME type. An image with JavaScript will never be executed as a script!

slides.title: X-Frame-Options: Clickjacking Defense
slides.content:
# Clickjacking Defense: `X-Frame-Options` 🖼️

As covered in CSRF, `X-Frame-Options` prevents your pages from being framed inside hostile iframes.

```http_not
// Forbid all framing:
X-Frame-Options: DENY

// Permit framing by same origin only:
X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN
```

Always pair with CSP's modern equivalent:

```http_not
Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self';
```

slides.title: Referrer-Policy Header
slides.content:
# Controlling URL Leaks: `Referrer-Policy` 🧭

When a user clicks a link from your site to an external site, the browser sends the `Referer` header containing your full page URL.

## The Danger of URL Leakage

If your URL contains sensitive data (`https://site.com/reset-password?token=secret123`), that secret token is leaked in plaintext to third-party servers!

## Recommended Header Value

```http_not
Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin
```

## How It Behaves:

- Same-origin requests: Sends full URL (`https://site.com/path?query`).
- Cross-origin HTTPS to HTTPS: Sends **origin only** (`https://site.com/`). Query parameters are stripped!
- Cross-origin HTTPS to HTTP: Sends **no referrer at all** (prevents downgrades).

slides.title: Permissions-Policy (Feature-Policy)
slides.content:
# Restricting Hardware APIs: `Permissions-Policy` 🎙️📷

The `Permissions-Policy` header (formerly `Feature-Policy`) allows web administrators to selectively enable, disable, and restrict browser hardware and sensor features.

```http_not
Permissions-Policy: geolocation=(), camera=(), microphone=(), payment=(self)
```

## What this Policy Enforces:

- `geolocation=()`: Geolocation is disabled for ALL scripts and iframes on this page.
- `camera=()`, `microphone=()`: Disables webcam and microphone access entirely.
- `payment=(self)`: Allows the Web Payments API only from the site's own origin.

> ⚡ **Defense in Depth:** Even if an attacker injects XSS or rogue advertising scripts, they cannot secretly turn on the victim's microphone or webcam!

slides.title: Cross-Origin Isolation: COOP and COEP
slides.content:
# Cross-Origin Isolation: COOP & COEP 🧱

To defend against microarchitectural CPU attacks like **Spectre**, high-performance web features like `SharedArrayBuffer` require **Cross-Origin Isolation**.

## 1. Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy (COOP)

Isolates your browsing context group from other origin windows (`window.opener` becomes null):

```http_not
Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin
```

## 2. Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy (COEP)

Prevents a document from loading any cross-origin resources that haven't explicitly granted permission (via CORP or CORS):

```http_not
Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp
```

slides.title: Testing Security Headers: SecurityHeaders.com
slides.content:
# Auditing Your Security Posture 🔍

You can audit any public website's security headers using free industry scanning tools like **SecurityHeaders.com** (founded by Scott Helme).

## Scoring Ladder (A+ to F)

- **A+ Grade**: Requires CSP without `'unsafe-inline'`, HSTS with preload, `nosniff`, `SAMEORIGIN`, and strict `Referrer-Policy`.
- **F Grade**: Missing all security headers; entirely vulnerable to clickjacking and MIME attacks.

Implementing Headers in Node.js with Helmet
Real-World Golden Standard Header Suite
slides.content:
# Production-Grade Security Header Suite 🏆

Here is the golden standard security header configuration for modern web applications:

```http_not
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN
Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin
Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), payment=(self)
Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-rAnd0m123'; object-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'self'; base-uri 'self';
```

slides.title: Common Header Misconfigurations
slides.content:
# Top Header Misconfigurations ⚠️

1. **Using `'unsafe-inline'` in script-src**: Defeats the primary purpose of CSP.
2. **Omitting `includeSubDomains` on HSTS**: Leaves subdomains vulnerable to SSL stripping attacks.
3. **Setting `X-Frame-Options` without CSP `frame-ancestors`**: Inconsistent support across modern browser engines.
4. **Missing `object-src 'none'`**: Leaves doors open for legacy Flash/Java plugin exploits.

slides.title: Summary: Security Headers
slides.content:
# Security Headers: Summary 📋

## Key Takeaways
- **CSP**: Enforces strict boundaries on executable scripts, styles, and origins.
- **HSTS**: Forces HTTPS across domains and subdomains (`includeSubDomains; preload`).
- **X-Content-Type-Options**: `nosniff` prevents MIME confusion attacks.
- **Referrer-Policy**: `strict-origin-when-cross-origin` stops URL credential leakage.
- **Permissions-Policy**: Locks down access to camera, microphone, and geolocation.
- **Helmet**: The premier library for one-line header management in Node.js.
